Elliott Farms has a silo for storage. The silo is a right circular cylinder topped by a right circular cone, both having the same radius. The height of the cone is half the height of the cylinder. The diameter of the base of the silo is 10 meters and the height of the entire silo is 27 meters. What is the volume, in cubic meters, of the silo? Express your answer in terms of $\pi$.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a silo composed of a cylindrical lower part with a conical roof, and a vertical height marker labeled 27 meters spanning the whole silo. From the text, read that the base diameter is 10 meters, so the radius is 5 meters, and that the cone height is half the cylinder height. Let the cylinder height be h; then the cone height is h/2 and the total height is h+h/2=27, so h=18 and the cone height is 9. Compute the total volume as cylinder volume plus cone volume: pi(5^2)(18)+(1/3)pi(5^2)(9)=450pi+75pi=525pi.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the diagram depicts a single composite solid with a cone sitting on a cylinder, and the side bracket marks the total height as 27 meters. From the text, take the common diameter as 10 meters, so the common base area is pi(5^2)=25pi. Instead of finding and adding two full volumes separately, convert the silo to an equivalent cylinder with the same base area and an effective height. If the cylinder height is H, then the cone height is H/2, so the total height is 3H/2=27, giving H=18; the cone contributes only one-third of its height to volume, so the effective height is H+(1/3)(H/2)=H+H/6=7H/6=21. Multiply by the base area: 25pi*21=525pi.
